title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure at the front end of a deployment: an automated licence plate reader asserted a match between a plate and a stolen-vehicle record, and the match was wrong. The camera's image was of a Chevy Malibu while the plate was on a red Dodge Ram pickup, a discrepancy visible in the data the system itself produced. The error did not stay inside the software. It propagated into a traffic stop conducted at gunpoint, a K-9 release, an arrest, and charges of resisting arrest and obstruction.

The failure sits at the handoff between an automated alert and the officers who act on it. Nothing in the reporting shows a verification step between the alert and the stop, and the vehicle mismatch was the kind of check that would have caught it before anyone was pulled over. The department's own K-9 policy, which requires handlers to weigh the severity of the crime, threats, and whether a suspect is resisting or fleeing, is a second checkpoint that the reporting does not show being applied to the alert's reliability.

What is not established is whether the misread was a known limitation of the system, how often it produces such errors, or whether any officer involved acted with intent rather than on the alert as given. An internal investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and charges were later dropped, but neither outcome establishes what the camera got wrong or why.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop began after a FLOCK camera incorrectly flagged a stolen license plate. The camera image belonged to a Chevy Malibu, but the plate was seen on a red Dodge Ram pickup. Officers stopped the truck with guns drawn and ordered driver Brandon Upchurch out. He raised his hands, asked why he was stopped, and was told to get on the ground. A K-9 was then released, and Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction.

Officers later learned the plate information was wrong and the truck did not have a stolen plate. An officer described the alert as a misread. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene. Police said they believed he might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. Multiple officers are under investigation, and the department's K-9 policy requires handlers to consider the crime's severity, threats, and whether a suspect is resisting or fleeing.
